s1.syndrome_frame: A toddler with a chronic skin eruption characterized by multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, accompanied by fever and otitis media
salient_findings: Multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale
Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm on histopathology
Positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163
key_facts: The patient is a toddler with a 2-month history of skin eruption
The eruption began with multiple round red patches that slowly increased in size
The patient has a medical history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and juvenile xanthogranulomas
The patient was treated with griseofulvin and clotrimazole without improvement
The patient developed fever and was diagnosed with otitis media one day prior to presentation
The patient is currently taking acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and amoxicillin
Scattered café au lait macules are present on the back
Histopathology showed a perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163
The white blood cell count is 76,400/µL
